newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP raises spectre of more steel job cuts.
newsitem.headline: BHP raises spectre of more steel job cuts.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd on Tuesday raised the spectre of up to 2,000 job losses at its Port Kembla steelworks in New South Wales over the next three years.
BHP said the steelworks, which now run on a work force of 7,000, would only need 5,000 if world productivity benchmarks were met.
BHP is striving to reach the benchmark of 1,000 tonnes of steel per year per worker.
Port Kembla aims to reach five million tonnes of steel production a year from 4.5 million now by the year 2000.
"That's 5,000 people," BHP Steel chief executive Ron McNeilly said at a news conference.
"It's very clear that integrated steel plants must drive for productivity levels of 1,000 tonnes per person per year," McNeilly said.
He said South Korea's Pohang Iron and Steel Co Ltd was already producing at the benchmark level and that Taiwan's China Steel Corp aimed to reach that level by the year 2000.
